subjects.description: small green rectangular mass attached to the bottom of a vertical spring

observation.what_happens: A small green block hung from a vertical spring oscillates up and down above a black-and-white striped bar. The motion is ongoing throughout the clip, starting near the top of the travel and still oscillating at the end.

calibration.note: scale from the fall itself: 1 px/s² over 1 arc = g of 9.807 m/s²

given: g = 9.807 m/s² (Earth); it set the scale, so treat g as known and fixed
reasoning: The path is straight vertical with s spanning 0-1300 and period ~0.58 s, so omega ~10.8 rad/s around ~650, with peaks slowly shrinking. These candidates test no loss vs linear viscous loss vs extra quadratic drag vs cubic spring nonlinearity.

caveats: Rest position sits far outside the seen travel, so stiffness and rest length trade off.
Only up-down motion was tracked and any sideways wobble was ignored.
critique.finding: The block hangs on a spring that pulls with stiffness {omega0} around rest length {s_nat} under gravity {g} with gentle drag {gamma}. That drag slowly shrinks the bounces and keeps matching the later motion.
critique.headline: Green block rides a spring, slowly settling.
critique.why_it_won: It lets the bounces gently shrink with damping, while the undamped spring keeps swinging too tall and the fancier drag versions wobble off track.

headline: Green block rides a spring, slowly settling.
finding: The block hangs on a spring that pulls with stiffness 11.2 ± 4.44e-4 1/s around rest length 463 m under gravity 9.81 m/s^2 with gentle drag 0.35 ± 8.49e-4 1/s. That drag slowly shrinks the bounces and keeps matching the later motion.

eyeball.confidence: low - only single still frame available, scale inferred from striped bar assuming 10 cm segments and typical lab spring; period and damping guessed from typical soft spring behavior
eyeball.law_in_words: vertical mass on spring with s measured downward from support: d2s/dt2 + gamma*ds/dt + omega0^2*(s - s_nat) - g = 0, where omega0^2 = k/m, gamma = c/m, s_nat is mass position when spring is unstretched
